head_commit.message:
feat: polish batch — letters sweep, cache keys, contrast, ai-status, italian tells, autopilot dates (#989)

* feat(autopilot): thread the job posting's publish date into found jobs

Adds FoundJob.posted_at (epoch ms, serde-defaulted so legacy records load
unchanged) alongside found_at, copies it from JobPosting in build_found_job,
and backfills/refreshes it in merge_found_jobs on re-surface using the same
fill-without-clobbering pattern as board/description/salary. Hand-syncs the
TS AutopilotFoundJob.postedAt contract (response types aren't gen:ipc'd).

feat: polish batch — letters sweep, cache keys, contrast, ai-status, italian tells, autopilot dates (#989)

* feat(autopilot): thread the job posting's publish date into found jobs

Adds FoundJob.posted_at (epoch ms, serde-defaulted so legacy records load
unchanged) alongside found_at, copies it from JobPosting in build_found_job,
and backfills/refreshes it in merge_found_jobs on re-surface using the same
fill-without-clobbering pattern as board/description/salary. Hand-syncs the
TS AutopilotFoundJob.postedAt contract (response types aren't gen:ipc'd).
Sort order (by_rank) is untouched per ADR-020 addendum.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ui): extend light-scheme opacity remap past the /20-/50 enumeration

text-foreground/NN and border-foreground/NN are Tailwind opacity-suffix
utilities compiled to literal escaped selectors over --color-foreground.
utilities.css only remapped /20-/50 for light; every other value in use
rendered at its raw alpha, near-invisible on light's near-black ink
(border-foreground had ZERO coverage: /10-/25 raw ~1.2-1.7:1).

Central-only fix: add text-foreground/15 and /55 (the only two escaped
values below the point where raw alpha already clears 4.5:1 on light),
plus a new border-foreground/10,/12,/15,/20,/25 block. /60+ (text) and
/70 (border) are deliberately left unmapped — already >=AA/3:1 raw, so
remapping them would only re-tint hundreds of call sites for no gain.
Components keep their existing classes.

Pins the fix with a red-first contrast seam test (independently
recomputes WCAG contrast from the literal color-mix % in the
stylesheet) plus a duplicate-rule guard, mirroring the existing
light-scheme-contrast.test.ts pattern.

* fix(dashboard): AI-status widget reads the active provider, not Ollama only

daemon regardless of which provider is actually active, so a user on
OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/a CLI agent — with local Ollama simply not
running — saw a false "AI Model not available" despite a fully
configured model.

Frontend-only fix (no src-tauri change needed): the AI-model row now
reads `useCanUseAI()` (already the app-wide, provider-kind-aware
readiness source used by ModelSelector/Analyze/TailorFlow/resume
builder) and `useSelectedModel()` for the detail label, instead of the
Ollama-only `h.ai` field. Reuses the existing `aiSetup.*` copy for the
blocked reasons (addApiKey/selectModel/installCli) — no new i18n keys.

Pinned with a red-first test suite that keeps the mocked Ollama probe
reporting `ready: false` throughout, proving the row no longer depends
on it.

* fix(cover-letter): add provider + model to the company_brief cache key

The company_brief KvCache row was keyed on company name alone, so a
user who switched AI models kept getting the OLD model's cached brief
for the full 7-day TTL. ADR-017 key discipline (StageIdentity
precedent, #985): anything that reaches the provider and changes the
answer belongs in the key — the brief is the direct output of the
active provider's own model doing web search + synthesis
(Completer::research), so provider + model are cache-key terms.

Checked salary_research for the same gap: it has it too, but
SalaryResearch::enrich is generic over a SalarySearcher trait (for
testability without a live AppHandle) which exposes no
provider_id()/model(), so it isn't the same one-line fix — flagging
as a follow-up rather than fixing it here.

* fix(ai): distinguish a rejected health probe from "still checking"

PR #989 CodeRabbit round 1, two MAJOR findings.

1. useCanUseAI read only `useSystemHealth().data`, never `isError`. A
   REJECTED health query (network blip, backend hiccup) leaves `data`
   undefined forever (retry: false) — indistinguishable from "still
   pending" in the local-server branch (permanent, silent "checking"
   that never resolves) and silently misreported as `installCli` ("go
   install the CLI") in the cli-agent branch, since `?? false` treated
   undefined-from-error the same as undefined-from-loading. A consumer
   rendering AiSetupHint with no reason then fell back to its own
   default (`aiSetup.addApiKey`) — wrong for every affected provider
   kind. Now three-way: pending (no reason, "checking") → error (new
   `healthUnavailable` reason) → settled (the real gate). New
   aiSetup.healthUnavailable en+de keys ("Couldn't check AI status. Try
   again in a moment." / "KI-Status konnte nicht geprüft werden.
   Versuche es in Kürze erneut."), wired into both AiSetupHint's
   MESSAGE_KEY and AISystemStatus's own copy.

2. AISystemStatus.test.tsx's reason→key table (added when `startOllama`
   shipped) never grew a row for it — a silent AI_REASON_KEY drift back
   to the addApiKey fallback would have stayed green. Adds both the
   startOllama and the new healthUnavailable rows.

Coverage: useCanUseAI.test.tsx gains a rejected-health-query case for
both consuming branches (local-server, cli-agent).

Mutation-tested per the coordinator's exact asks: dropping startOllama
from AI_REASON_KEY turns its table row red (falls back to addApiKey);
disabling the isError checks turns both rejected-query tests red

head_commit.message:
feat(export): phase 8 — sidebar and monogram letter layouts, and a reachable letter ATS toggle (#988)

* feat(export): add the sidebar and monogram cover-letter layouts

Two new arrangements alongside Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy, each with a DOCX
approximation and an honest ATS-mode degradation.

Sidebar widens the left margin to 62mm, fills it with a pale accent rail, and
`place`s the letterhead (name/role/contact) into it; the correspondence runs in
ONE column beside it. The rail is a margin position, not a second column of
prose, so extraction still reads letterhead -> date -> recipient -> body ->
sign-off. `place` does not participate in layout, so the rail can never push the
body around or move a page break.

Monogram sets a pale accent square carrying up to two initials beside a
name/role/contact lockup, over a rule. The square is pale-fill with accent ink
rather than a saturated tile with white text, because the accent comes from
whichever resume template is active and a light accent would put white on
near-white -- and the 85% lightening is the same `band_tint_hex` the DOCX side
already uses, which is what lets the two formats show one tint.

The brief said to mirror how Banded gates its band under ats_mode. It does not:
`ats_mode` never reached the letter path at all. `render_letter_pdf` had no
`ats` parameter, `LetterOpts` had no `ats` field, and `pdf/mod.rs` read
`request.ats_mode` for resumes only -- so a user who turned the toggle on still
exported a banded cover letter with its band. That is threaded now, as
`data.opts.ats`, and Banded's band is gated on it too: the discipline has to be
uniform or the toggle is a lie. Under ATS mode Sidebar drops the rail and stacks
the letterhead in one plain column, Monogram drops the device entirely (its
initials are real text -- extraction read "JS Jane Smith", two characters of
noise ahead of the candidate's own name), and Banded drops the band. No layout
adds or removes a WORD either way, which is what the tests assert alongside the
missing fill.

`ats` is a required parameter on `parse_cover_letter` rather than a defaulted
field: an ATS toggle that silently fails to reach the renderer looks exactly
like one that works, which is how this gap survived four letter layouts.

Structural elements gate on `data.opts`, never on the layout id -- the DE DIN
Betreff renders and the US subject does not, from the identical layout.

DOCX: `LetterDocxStyle` gains rows for both, read off each `.typ` feature by
feature. Sidebar's rail has no DOCX equivalent at all (a text box or a
two-column table would be exactly the multi-column trap the export avoids), so
it becomes the same shaded name paragraph Banded uses, with the contact LEFT at
the margin. That alignment is why `contact_align` is now a stored field instead
of a function of "centred or right": Sidebar and Monogram left-align the contact
while leaving the name left too, which the derived version could not express --
and inherit-by-omission is the defect that took four review rounds on Navy.
Monogram's device becomes a shaded RUN at the head of the name paragraph, from
the SAME `monogram_initials` the `.typ` reads via `LetterHead.initials`, so the
two formats cannot disagree about what it says and both extract "JS Jane Smith"
rather than putting the initials on a line of their own.

`monogram_initials` is Rust, not Typst, because every interesting case is string
handling a `.typ` cannot be tested on: first + LAST token (so "Jane van der
Berg" is JB, not JV), letterless tokens skipped ("Jane (she/her) Smith" is JS),
non-ASCII capitals preserved, and a hard two-character cap so a long name can
never overflow the fixed-size square.

Also replaces `letter_template_sources()`, which returned a fixed tuple of three
layout sources and went stale the moment Navy was added -- the preview generator
could not reach the newest layout at all, and being `#[ignore]`d nothing
noticed. It now routes through the production picker.

Tracking is 0.04em on both new names, inside the 0.03-0.10em band every template
here uses. The accented-Latin extraction guard that caught Cologne Navy's 0.14em
("A LVA R O  E S P O S I T O") now covers both.

Verified: the rail placement is measured against the RENDERED page rather than
trusted -- leftmost glyph exactly at the 7mm rail padding, nothing in the
rail/body gutter, body column at 62mm, and nothing left of 25.4mm under ATS
mode. A sign error in the `place` offsets would pass every text-only assertion.
All three ATS gates were mutation-tested: forcing `ats` false in each `.typ`
fails the corresponding test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(export): register the sidebar and monogram letter layouts in the ui

The renderer half of the two new arrangements: the wire union in the shared IPC
contract, the ordered id list the picker and its roving-tabindex both walk, two
picker options, and en/de strings.

Five registration points exist per letter layout, traced end-to-end from how
Navy is wired: (1) the Rust `LetterLayout` enum + its kebab-case deserialize arm
+ the round-trip table, (2) the `.typ` asset plus the `include_str!` const and
`letter_source` picker arm, (3) the DOCX `LetterDocxStyle` row and dispatch arm,
(4) this `LetterLayoutId` union in `packages/shared`, and (5) the renderer's
`LETTER_LAYOUT_IDS` + picker options + translations. Miss (4) and a stale
frontend id degrades to Classic silently; miss (5) and the layout exists in the
backend but nobody can pick it.

The picker previously had no guard tying its own `LAYOUTS` array to
`LETTER_LAYOUT_IDS`, even though the keyboard handler walks the latter while the
render walks the former. A layout in one and not the other is invisible, and one
in a different position makes ArrowDown jump to an option that is not next on
screen. Both are now a test failure; verified by deleting the monogram entry.

The "pairs with ..." wording in the descriptions is deliberate. Layout and
resume template are orthogonal axes in this app -- a layout inherits whichever
palette is active via `style_from_template`, so Sidebar under Regent gets
Regent's burgundy rail. The strings suggest a pairing (Sidebar with the sidebar
families Atelier/Aria/Saffron/Deedy, Monogram with the bold-header families
Awesome/Jake/Throughline) without coupling anything, which is the same posture
Navy's "Pairs with Cologne Navy" already takes.

Both descriptions state that the decoration is dropped in ATS mode, so the
degradation is discoverable before export rather than a surprise in the output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): stop the new letter layouts hyphenating, mis-reading names and claiming din

Review round 1 on the sidebar/monogram layouts. Five findings, all in the two
files this PR added.

Hyphenation (ruling 1, scoped): both new layouts now set `hyphenate: false`.
Typst turns hyphenation on with `justify`, and a hyphenated break puts a real
break in the PDF text layer -- "microservices architecture" extracts as
"architec-ture" and an ATS tokenising on whitespace loses the keyword. Justify
stays. The guard lives in `letter_lower`, the choke point every extraction in
this file already flows through, so no test can regress it -- but gated on a
`NO_SOFT_HYPHEN_LAYOUTS` roster of the two new layouts, because the four SHIPPED
ones still hyphenate and a family-wide assert would go red on them today. The
roster grows when the sweep lands.

Correcting my own measurement, per the critic: of the three U+00AD-adjacent
breaks I reported, only ONE is a genuine soft-hyphen break. The others are hard
hyphens ("end-to-end"), which Typst tags with /ActualText and a conforming
extractor recovers -- asserting on those would be asserting on a non-defect, so
the guard checks U+00AD only. And the shipped family is SIX .typ files, not the
five I wrote: letter_navy.typ was already there.

Initials, two defects in one function. It searched each token for its first
alphanumeric ANYWHERE, so a token that merely contained a letter contributed
one: "Jane Smith (they/them)" was JT. And it had no notion of a title, so
"Dr. Jane Smith" was DS and the German "Dipl.-Ing. Max Müller" was DM. A token
now has to START with an alphanumeric, and a token that abbreviates a WORD (two
or more letters before its period) is a title or qualification and is dropped --
while a single-letter initial keeps counting, so "J. Smith" stays JS instead of
degrading to S.

My test for the first of those was a false positive and the critic was right
about why: the fixture was "(she/her)" and the expected "JS" is ALSO what the
broken code produced, because its S came from "she". Refixtured to
"(they/them)", where correct and broken are distinguishable (JS vs JT), which is
what made the mutation run meaningful.

Device on a letterhead-less letter: the PDF-side name falls back to the first
LINE when no candidate name is supplied, and three renderer call sites pass an
empty one -- so on a letter that opens at the salutation the device rendered
"DM", from "Dear Hiring Manager,". Reproduced exactly. The DOCX renderer already
refused to treat an opening line as a name; `letterhead_initials` is the PDF
side of the same guard, scoped to the DEVICE because what `letterhead.name`
should show there is a separate pre-existing question across all six layouts.

Sidebar's contact links go through `place()` with a negative dx into the margin,
which is the documented annotation-loss shape. They survive -- but nothing said
so, and a dropped /Annots entry is invisible to every text assertion, so it is
pinned now in both modes.

DIN 5008: the header claimed market conventions were honoured while the
recipient block sits at 62mm, so a DE letter cannot show its address through a
window envelope. Chose the honest comment over a locale-conditional rail, and
not only because that is heavy -- it is unachievable. Form B needs the
Anschriftenfeld clear from 20mm, and a rail narrower than that cannot hold a
contact line at 9.5pt. DIN compliance and a contact rail want the same strip of
paper, so Sidebar is a screen/attachment layout and the comment now says to pick
Classic or Navy for the envelope.

Also: the monogram device was a bound `#let`, so it read
`data.letterhead.initials` when the binding evaluated -- before the
`"initials" in data.letterhead` check below it. The guard was dead. It takes the
initials as a parameter now, so the read happens only on the checked branch.

Every new guard was mutation-tested: removing `hyphenate: false` fails four
tests, the old token rule fails the pronoun and title tests (DS vs JS), removing
the salutation guard yields DM and MG, and dropping the `link()` wrapper fails
with `found []`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(shared): export the letter-layout id union from the contracts barrel

`TemplateId` is re-exported here and the renderer imports it instead of keeping
a hand-synced copy, precisely so adding an id on one side surfaces as a `tsc`
failure rather than compiling as a silent subset. The letter-layout union had no
such export, which is why the renderer carried a second copy of it.

Type-only and additive. The matching renderer-side switch (importing the union
from `@ajh/shared` rather than redeclaring it) is applied in the working tree
and typechecks, but is NOT in this commit: a frontend-author is editing that
same file in parallel for the ats-toggle work, and staging it here would sweep
their uncommitted changes into my commit. It rides along with theirs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(export): pass cover-letter render knobs as a struct, not eight positionals

Removes all five `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` this PR had added, but
the lint was the symptom. The real defect it was silencing:

    render_letter_pdf(text, template, contact, meta_name, market, lang, …)
    generate_cover_letter_docx(text, meta, template, contact, lang, market, …)

`market` and `lang` are both `&str`, adjacent, and the two renderers took them
in OPPOSITE orders. Swapping them compiles silently and produces a letter with
the wrong page size and the wrong date convention — a US-shaped German letter,
from a typo the compiler cannot see. `LetterRender { market, lang, layout, ats }`
makes that unrepresentable.

Applied to the four eight-parameter entry points (`render_letter_pdf`,
`render_letter_svg_pages`, `build_letter_world`, and both DOCX letter fns).
`parse_cover_letter` deliberately keeps its positional parameters: it is at
seven, under the lint's threshold, it has no use for `layout`, and pulling it in
would have forced sixteen parser tests to name a layout they do not exercise.

Behaviour-preserving. The proof is the preview generator: re-running
`generate_cover_template_previews` reproduces all sixteen committed SVGs
byte-identically, which it can only do if the letter world is built from exactly
the same inputs as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ui): make the cover-letter ATS toggle reachable

No cover-letter surface exposed an ATS toggle, so the new Monogram layout put
"JS " in front of the candidate's own name in the text layer with no off switch,
and the shipped Sidebar/Monogram copy promised a switch that did not exist. Two
gates were responsible: every toggle render site was resume-only
(`!isCover && isDesignTier`, `activeOut === 'resume' && ...`), and all five
force-clear sites wiped atsMode the moment an ATS-TIER resume template was
picked -- which is exactly the case where the letter is the only document the
flag still drives.

NO new wire flag. `BaseExportRequest.atsMode` already travels per DOCUMENT (one
request carries one document), and after the Rust threading the letter reads the
same field as `data.opts.ats`. A second `letterAtsMode` would only be needed if
one request carried both documents. The only `packages/shared` edit is the
`atsMode` JSDoc, which now states both halves of the semantics; no type changed.

Semantics: atsMode is ONE per-export flag, and a surface shows the switch when
the flag can still change the document on screen -- resume via `isDesignTier`
(unchanged; a documented no-op for ATS-tier templates per single_column.typ),
letter via the new `isDecoratedLetterLayout`. `shouldClearAtsMode` replaces the
bare `!isDesignTier(id)` at all five clear sites and refuses to clear while a
decorated letter is reading the flag.

`isDecoratedLetterLayout` is a `Record<LetterLayoutId, boolean>` mirroring the
`ats` gates in the .typ files one for one, so a new layout id fails tsc until
someone decides whether it degrades. Navy is deliberately FALSE despite being a
"design" arrangement: `letter_navy.typ` has no ats gate, so a toggle there would
be a switch that changes nothing. Classic/Refined likewise.

Three letter surfaces render the layout picker, so all three get the toggle:
StepTemplate (its card switch now carries one hint line per affected document,
so a 'both' run with a design-tier template states both effects), and
GenerationOutput + OutputPanelDone via a new shared `AtsModeToggle` -- extracted
from GenerationOutput's inline block rather than copied, so the two toolbar
strips cannot drift in markup or a11y wiring. OutputPanelDone matters most: it
REPLACES the wizard once a run is done, so a Monogram picked there previously
had no undo short of regenerating.

Copy: new `atsModeHintLetter` (en+de) naming the three decorations. The layout
descriptions now say "dropped by ATS-safe mode" instead of "in ATS mode" so the
promise names the control the user has to find, and Banded finally says it too
(its band became ats-gated in this branch).

Tests, each mutation-verified by reverting the guard it covers:
- `isDecoratedLetterLayout` / `shouldClearAtsMode` incl. the review's worst case
  (ATS-tier template + monogram must NOT clear).
- Toggle visible on banded/sidebar/monogram, absent on classic/refined/navy, on
  all three surfaces; absent on the resume tab; absent when the host owns no
  atsMode setter.
- The flag survives to the wire: exportPDF puts `atsMode` on a COVER-LETTER
  request, and useTailorGeneration carries the host's atsMode onto that call
  alongside the layout -- so flipping the switch really changes the export.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ui): anchor, name, announce and release the ATS toggle

Five ui-ux-expert findings on the reachable cover-letter ATS toggle.

1 (HIGH) StepTemplate's switch row was `items-center`. With BOTH hint lines up
  -- the design-tier resume + decorated letter case the previous commit added --
  free-wrapping 10px German copy grows the row to ~80-90px and floats the 16px
  track that far below the label it belongs to. `items-start` anchors it. jsdom
  zeroes rects, so the guard is a class assertion on the row.

2 The two hints both opened "Recommended for ATS submissions --" and read as one
  line printed twice. Each now leads with its document ("Resume: ...", "Cover
  letter: ...", "Lebenslauf:"/"Anschreiben:" in de, Sie-form kept) and the
  shared preamble moves to the end of the resume lines. Neither line said the
  switch drives BOTH documents, so `atsModeHintBothDocs` says it -- rendered
  only when both actually apply, where the ambiguity exists.

3 The switch had no aria-label, so its accessible name was the label plus every
  hint concatenated. Now `aria-label` + `aria-describedby`, which is what the
  @ajh/ui Switch primitive already does with its own description. The describedby
  ids are emitted under the SAME guard as the lines they point at. The old test
  used a /partial/ name match that passed either way; it now asserts the EXACT
  accessible name, plus that every referenced id resolves.

4 Nothing announced the toggle's ARRIVAL at the two toolbar surfaces (StepTemplate
  sits inside GenerateWizard's aria-live wrapper; these do not) -- a screen-reader
  user picked Monogram and got silence. Both now carry SectionTimeline's pattern:
  an always-mounted `role="status"` sr-only region, empty while hidden. Always
  mounted because a live region cannot announce its own first render, and sr-only
  because it is out of flow -- the toolbar's gap is unchanged.

5 The stale-flag round-trip was real: decorated layout + ATS on -> switch to

head_commit.message:
feat(export): phase 8 — sidebar and monogram letter layouts, and a reachable letter ATS toggle (#988)

* feat(export): add the sidebar and monogram cover-letter layouts

Two new arrangements alongside Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy, each with a DOCX
approximation and an honest ATS-mode degradation.

Sidebar widens the left margin to 62mm, fills it with a pale accent rail, and
`place`s the letterhead (name/role/contact) into it; the correspondence runs in
ONE column beside it. The rail is a margin position, not a second column of
prose, so extraction still reads letterhead -> date -> recipient -> body ->
sign-off. `place` does not participate in layout, so the rail can never push the
body around or move a page break.

Monogram sets a pale accent square carrying up to two initials beside a
name/role/contact lockup, over a rule. The square is pale-fill with accent ink
rather than a saturated tile with white text, because the accent comes from
whichever resume template is active and a light accent would put white on
near-white -- and the 85% lightening is the same `band_tint_hex` the DOCX side
already uses, which is what lets the two formats show one tint.

The brief said to mirror how Banded gates its band under ats_mode. It does not:
`ats_mode` never reached the letter path at all. `render_letter_pdf` had no
`ats` parameter, `LetterOpts` had no `ats` field, and `pdf/mod.rs` read
`request.ats_mode` for resumes only -- so a user who turned the toggle on still
exported a banded cover letter with its band. That is threaded now, as
`data.opts.ats`, and Banded's band is gated on it too: the discipline has to be
uniform or the toggle is a lie. Under ATS mode Sidebar drops the rail and stacks
the letterhead in one plain column, Monogram drops the device entirely (its
initials are real text -- extraction read "JS Jane Smith", two characters of
noise ahead of the candidate's own name), and Banded drops the band. No layout
adds or removes a WORD either way, which is what the tests assert alongside the
missing fill.

`ats` is a required parameter on `parse_cover_letter` rather than a defaulted
field: an ATS toggle that silently fails to reach the renderer looks exactly
like one that works, which is how this gap survived four letter layouts.

Structural elements gate on `data.opts`, never on the layout id -- the DE DIN
Betreff renders and the US subject does not, from the identical layout.

DOCX: `LetterDocxStyle` gains rows for both, read off each `.typ` feature by
feature. Sidebar's rail has no DOCX equivalent at all (a text box or a
two-column table would be exactly the multi-column trap the export avoids), so
it becomes the same shaded name paragraph Banded uses, with the contact LEFT at
the margin. That alignment is why `contact_align` is now a stored field instead
of a function of "centred or right": Sidebar and Monogram left-align the contact
while leaving the name left too, which the derived version could not express --
and inherit-by-omission is the defect that took four review rounds on Navy.
Monogram's device becomes a shaded RUN at the head of the name paragraph, from
the SAME `monogram_initials` the `.typ` reads via `LetterHead.initials`, so the
two formats cannot disagree about what it says and both extract "JS Jane Smith"
rather than putting the initials on a line of their own.

`monogram_initials` is Rust, not Typst, because every interesting case is string
handling a `.typ` cannot be tested on: first + LAST token (so "Jane van der
Berg" is JB, not JV), letterless tokens skipped ("Jane (she/her) Smith" is JS),
non-ASCII capitals preserved, and a hard two-character cap so a long name can
never overflow the fixed-size square.

Also replaces `letter_template_sources()`, which returned a fixed tuple of three
layout sources and went stale the moment Navy was added -- the preview generator
could not reach the newest layout at all, and being `#[ignore]`d nothing
noticed. It now routes through the production picker.

Tracking is 0.04em on both new names, inside the 0.03-0.10em band every template
here uses. The accented-Latin extraction guard that caught Cologne Navy's 0.14em
("A LVA R O  E S P O S I T O") now covers both.

Verified: the rail placement is measured against the RENDERED page rather than
trusted -- leftmost glyph exactly at the 7mm rail padding, nothing in the
rail/body gutter, body column at 62mm, and nothing left of 25.4mm under ATS
mode. A sign error in the `place` offsets would pass every text-only assertion.
All three ATS gates were mutation-tested: forcing `ats` false in each `.typ`
fails the corresponding test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(export): register the sidebar and monogram letter layouts in the ui

The renderer half of the two new arrangements: the wire union in the shared IPC
contract, the ordered id list the picker and its roving-tabindex both walk, two
picker options, and en/de strings.

Five registration points exist per letter layout, traced end-to-end from how
Navy is wired: (1) the Rust `LetterLayout` enum + its kebab-case deserialize arm
+ the round-trip table, (2) the `.typ` asset plus the `include_str!` const and
`letter_source` picker arm, (3) the DOCX `LetterDocxStyle` row and dispatch arm,
(4) this `LetterLayoutId` union in `packages/shared`, and (5) the renderer's
`LETTER_LAYOUT_IDS` + picker options + translations. Miss (4) and a stale
frontend id degrades to Classic silently; miss (5) and the layout exists in the
backend but nobody can pick it.

The picker previously had no guard tying its own `LAYOUTS` array to
`LETTER_LAYOUT_IDS`, even though the keyboard handler walks the latter while the
render walks the former. A layout in one and not the other is invisible, and one
in a different position makes ArrowDown jump to an option that is not next on
screen. Both are now a test failure; verified by deleting the monogram entry.

The "pairs with ..." wording in the descriptions is deliberate. Layout and
resume template are orthogonal axes in this app -- a layout inherits whichever
palette is active via `style_from_template`, so Sidebar under Regent gets
Regent's burgundy rail. The strings suggest a pairing (Sidebar with the sidebar
families Atelier/Aria/Saffron/Deedy, Monogram with the bold-header families
Awesome/Jake/Throughline) without coupling anything, which is the same posture
Navy's "Pairs with Cologne Navy" already takes.

Both descriptions state that the decoration is dropped in ATS mode, so the
degradation is discoverable before export rather than a surprise in the output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): stop the new letter layouts hyphenating, mis-reading names and claiming din

Review round 1 on the sidebar/monogram layouts. Five findings, all in the two
files this PR added.

Hyphenation (ruling 1, scoped): both new layouts now set `hyphenate: false`.
Typst turns hyphenation on with `justify`, and a hyphenated break puts a real
break in the PDF text layer -- "microservices architecture" extracts as
"architec-ture" and an ATS tokenising on whitespace loses the keyword. Justify
stays. The guard lives in `letter_lower`, the choke point every extraction in
this file already flows through, so no test can regress it -- but gated on a
`NO_SOFT_HYPHEN_LAYOUTS` roster of the two new layouts, because the four SHIPPED
ones still hyphenate and a family-wide assert would go red on them today. The
roster grows when the sweep lands.

Correcting my own measurement, per the critic: of the three U+00AD-adjacent
breaks I reported, only ONE is a genuine soft-hyphen break. The others are hard
hyphens ("end-to-end"), which Typst tags with /ActualText and a conforming
extractor recovers -- asserting on those would be asserting on a non-defect, so
the guard checks U+00AD only. And the shipped family is SIX .typ files, not the
five I wrote: letter_navy.typ was already there.

Initials, two defects in one function. It searched each token for its first
alphanumeric ANYWHERE, so a token that merely contained a letter contributed
one: "Jane Smith (they/them)" was JT. And it had no notion of a title, so
"Dr. Jane Smith" was DS and the German "Dipl.-Ing. Max Müller" was DM. A token
now has to START with an alphanumeric, and a token that abbreviates a WORD (two
or more letters before its period) is a title or qualification and is dropped --
while a single-letter initial keeps counting, so "J. Smith" stays JS instead of
degrading to S.

My test for the first of those was a false positive and the critic was right
about why: the fixture was "(she/her)" and the expected "JS" is ALSO what the
broken code produced, because its S came from "she". Refixtured to
"(they/them)", where correct and broken are distinguishable (JS vs JT), which is
what made the mutation run meaningful.

Device on a letterhead-less letter: the PDF-side name falls back to the first
LINE when no candidate name is supplied, and three renderer call sites pass an
empty one -- so on a letter that opens at the salutation the device rendered
"DM", from "Dear Hiring Manager,". Reproduced exactly. The DOCX renderer already
refused to treat an opening line as a name; `letterhead_initials` is the PDF
side of the same guard, scoped to the DEVICE because what `letterhead.name`
should show there is a separate pre-existing question across all six layouts.

Sidebar's contact links go through `place()` with a negative dx into the margin,
which is the documented annotation-loss shape. They survive -- but nothing said
so, and a dropped /Annots entry is invisible to every text assertion, so it is
pinned now in both modes.

DIN 5008: the header claimed market conventions were honoured while the
recipient block sits at 62mm, so a DE letter cannot show its address through a
window envelope. Chose the honest comment over a locale-conditional rail, and
not only because that is heavy -- it is unachievable. Form B needs the
Anschriftenfeld clear from 20mm, and a rail narrower than that cannot hold a
contact line at 9.5pt. DIN compliance and a contact rail want the same strip of
paper, so Sidebar is a screen/attachment layout and the comment now says to pick
Classic or Navy for the envelope.

Also: the monogram device was a bound `#let`, so it read
`data.letterhead.initials` when the binding evaluated -- before the
`"initials" in data.letterhead` check below it. The guard was dead. It takes the
initials as a parameter now, so the read happens only on the checked branch.

Every new guard was mutation-tested: removing `hyphenate: false` fails four
tests, the old token rule fails the pronoun and title tests (DS vs JS), removing
the salutation guard yields DM and MG, and dropping the `link()` wrapper fails
with `found []`.

* refactor(export): pass cover-letter render knobs as a struct, not eight positionals

Removes all five `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` this PR had added, but
the lint was the symptom. The real defect it was silencing:

    render_letter_pdf(text, template, contact, meta_name, market, lang, …)
    generate_cover_letter_docx(text, meta, template, contact, lang, market, …)

`market` and `lang` are both `&str`, adjacent, and the two renderers took them
in OPPOSITE orders. Swapping them compiles silently and produces a letter with
the wrong page size and the wrong date convention — a US-shaped German letter,
from a typo the compiler cannot see. `LetterRender { market, lang, layout, ats }`
makes that unrepresentable.

Applied to the four eight-parameter entry points (`render_letter_pdf`,
`render_letter_svg_pages`, `build_letter_world`, and both DOCX letter fns).
`parse_cover_letter` deliberately keeps its positional parameters: it is at
seven, under the lint's threshold, it has no use for `layout`, and pulling it in
would have forced sixteen parser tests to name a layout they do not exercise.

Behaviour-preserving. The proof is the preview generator: re-running
`generate_cover_template_previews` reproduces all sixteen committed SVGs
byte-identically, which it can only do if the letter world is built from exactly

head_commit.message:
feat(export): phase 8 — sidebar and monogram letter layouts, and a reachable letter ATS toggle (#988)

* feat(export): add the sidebar and monogram cover-letter layouts

Two new arrangements alongside Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy, each with a DOCX
approximation and an honest ATS-mode degradation.

Sidebar widens the left margin to 62mm, fills it with a pale accent rail, and
`place`s the letterhead (name/role/contact) into it; the correspondence runs in
ONE column beside it. The rail is a margin position, not a second column of
prose, so extraction still reads letterhead -> date -> recipient -> body ->
sign-off. `place` does not participate in layout, so the rail can never push the
body around or move a page break.

Monogram sets a pale accent square carrying up to two initials beside a
name/role/contact lockup, over a rule. The square is pale-fill with accent ink
rather than a saturated tile with white text, because the accent comes from
whichever resume template is active and a light accent would put white on
near-white -- and the 85% lightening is the same `band_tint_hex` the DOCX side
already uses, which is what lets the two formats show one tint.

The brief said to mirror how Banded gates its band under ats_mode. It does not:
`ats_mode` never reached the letter path at all. `render_letter_pdf` had no
`ats` parameter, `LetterOpts` had no `ats` field, and `pdf/mod.rs` read
`request.ats_mode` for resumes only -- so a user who turned the toggle on still
exported a banded cover letter with its band. That is threaded now, as
`data.opts.ats`, and Banded's band is gated on it too: the discipline has to be
uniform or the toggle is a lie. Under ATS mode Sidebar drops the rail and stacks
the letterhead in one plain column, Monogram drops the device entirely (its
initials are real text -- extraction read "JS Jane Smith", two characters of
noise ahead of the candidate's own name), and Banded drops the band. No layout
adds or removes a WORD either way, which is what the tests assert alongside the
missing fill.

`ats` is a required parameter on `parse_cover_letter` rather than a defaulted
field: an ATS toggle that silently fails to reach the renderer looks exactly
like one that works, which is how this gap survived four letter layouts.

Structural elements gate on `data.opts`, never on the layout id -- the DE DIN
Betreff renders and the US subject does not, from the identical layout.

DOCX: `LetterDocxStyle` gains rows for both, read off each `.typ` feature by
feature. Sidebar's rail has no DOCX equivalent at all (a text box or a
two-column table would be exactly the multi-column trap the export avoids), so
it becomes the same shaded name paragraph Banded uses, with the contact LEFT at
the margin. That alignment is why `contact_align` is now a stored field instead
of a function of "centred or right": Sidebar and Monogram left-align the contact
while leaving the name left too, which the derived version could not express --
and inherit-by-omission is the defect that took four review rounds on Navy.
Monogram's device becomes a shaded RUN at the head of the name paragraph, from
the SAME `monogram_initials` the `.typ` reads via `LetterHead.initials`, so the
two formats cannot disagree about what it says and both extract "JS Jane Smith"
rather than putting the initials on a line of their own.

`monogram_initials` is Rust, not Typst, because every interesting case is string
handling a `.typ` cannot be tested on: first + LAST token (so "Jane van der
Berg" is JB, not JV), letterless tokens skipped ("Jane (she/her) Smith" is JS),
non-ASCII capitals preserved, and a hard two-character cap so a long name can
never overflow the fixed-size square.

Also replaces `letter_template_sources()`, which returned a fixed tuple of three
layout sources and went stale the moment Navy was added -- the preview generator
could not reach the newest layout at all, and being `#[ignore]`d nothing
noticed. It now routes through the production picker.

Tracking is 0.04em on both new names, inside the 0.03-0.10em band every template
here uses. The accented-Latin extraction guard that caught Cologne Navy's 0.14em
("A LVA R O  E S P O S I T O") now covers both.

Verified: the rail placement is measured against the RENDERED page rather than
trusted -- leftmost glyph exactly at the 7mm rail padding, nothing in the
rail/body gutter, body column at 62mm, and nothing left of 25.4mm under ATS
mode. A sign error in the `place` offsets would pass every text-only assertion.
All three ATS gates were mutation-tested: forcing `ats` false in each `.typ`
fails the corresponding test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(export): register the sidebar and monogram letter layouts in the ui

The renderer half of the two new arrangements: the wire union in the shared IPC
contract, the ordered id list the picker and its roving-tabindex both walk, two
picker options, and en/de strings.

Five registration points exist per letter layout, traced end-to-end from how
Navy is wired: (1) the Rust `LetterLayout` enum + its kebab-case deserialize arm
+ the round-trip table, (2) the `.typ` asset plus the `include_str!` const and
`letter_source` picker arm, (3) the DOCX `LetterDocxStyle` row and dispatch arm,
(4) this `LetterLayoutId` union in `packages/shared`, and (5) the renderer's
`LETTER_LAYOUT_IDS` + picker options + translations. Miss (4) and a stale
frontend id degrades to Classic silently; miss (5) and the layout exists in the
backend but nobody can pick it.

The picker previously had no guard tying its own `LAYOUTS` array to
`LETTER_LAYOUT_IDS`, even though the keyboard handler walks the latter while the
render walks the former. A layout in one and not the other is invisible, and one
in a different position makes ArrowDown jump to an option that is not next on
screen. Both are now a test failure; verified by deleting the monogram entry.

The "pairs with ..." wording in the descriptions is deliberate. Layout and
resume template are orthogonal axes in this app -- a layout inherits whichever
palette is active via `style_from_template`, so Sidebar under Regent gets
Regent's burgundy rail. The strings suggest a pairing (Sidebar with the sidebar
families Atelier/Aria/Saffron/Deedy, Monogram with the bold-header families
Awesome/Jake/Throughline) without coupling anything, which is the same posture
Navy's "Pairs with Cologne Navy" already takes.

Both descriptions state that the decoration is dropped in ATS mode, so the
degradation is discoverable before export rather than a surprise in the output.

* fix(export): stop the new letter layouts hyphenating, mis-reading names and claiming din

Review round 1 on the sidebar/monogram layouts. Five findings, all in the two
files this PR added.

Hyphenation (ruling 1, scoped): both new layouts now set `hyphenate: false`.
Typst turns hyphenation on with `justify`, and a hyphenated break puts a real
break in the PDF text layer -- "microservices architecture" extracts as
"architec-ture" and an ATS tokenising on whitespace loses the keyword. Justify
stays. The guard lives in `letter_lower`, the choke point every extraction in
this file already flows through, so no test can regress it -- but gated on a
`NO_SOFT_HYPHEN_LAYOUTS` roster of the two new layouts, because the four SHIPPED
ones still hyphenate and a family-wide assert would go red on them today. The
roster grows when the sweep lands.

Correcting my own measurement, per the critic: of the three U+00AD-adjacent
breaks I reported, only ONE is a genuine soft-hyphen break. The others are hard
hyphens ("end-to-end"), which Typst tags with /ActualText and a conforming
extractor recovers -- asserting on those would be asserting on a non-defect, so
the guard checks U+00AD only. And the shipped family is SIX .typ files, not the
five I wrote: letter_navy.typ was already there.

Initials, two defects in one function. It searched each token for its first
alphanumeric ANYWHERE, so a token that merely contained a letter contributed
one: "Jane Smith (they/them)" was JT. And it had no notion of a title, so
"Dr. Jane Smith" was DS and the German "Dipl.-Ing. Max Müller" was DM. A token
now has to START with an alphanumeric, and a token that abbreviates a WORD (two
or more letters before its period) is a title or qualification and is dropped --
while a single-letter initial keeps counting, so "J. Smith" stays JS instead of
degrading to S.

My test for the first of those was a false positive and the critic was right
about why: the fixture was "(she/her)" and the expected "JS" is ALSO what the
broken code produced, because its S came from "she". Refixtured to
"(they/them)", where correct and broken are distinguishable (JS vs JT), which is
what made the mutation run meaningful.

Device on a letterhead-less letter: the PDF-side name falls back to the first

refused to treat an opening line as a name; `letterhead_initials` is the PDF
side of the same guard, scoped to the DEVICE because what `letterhead.name`
should show there is a separate pre-existing question across all six layouts.

which is the documented annotation-loss shape. They survive -- but nothing said
so, and a dropped /Annots entry is invisible to every text assertion, so it is
pinned now in both modes.

DIN 5008: the header claimed market conventions were honoured while the
recipient block sits at 62mm, so a DE letter cannot show its address through a
window envelope. Chose the honest comment over a locale-conditional rail, and
not only because that is heavy -- it is unachievable. Form B needs the
Anschriftenfeld clear from 20mm, and a rail narrower than that cannot hold a
contact line at 9.5pt. DIN compliance and a contact rail want the same strip of
paper, so Sidebar is a screen/attachment layout and the comment now says to pick
Classic or Navy for the envelope.

Also: the monogram device was a bound `#let`, so it read
`data.letterhead.initials` when the binding evaluated -- before the
`"initials" in data.letterhead` check below it. The guard was dead. It takes the
initials as a parameter now, so the read happens only on the checked branch.

Every new guard was mutation-tested: removing `hyphenate: false` fails four
tests, the old token rule fails the pronoun and title tests (DS vs JS), removing
the salutation guard yields DM and MG, and dropping the `link()` wrapper fails
with `found []`.

head_commit.message:
feat(export): phase 8 — sidebar and monogram letter layouts, and a reachable letter ATS toggle (#988)

* feat(export): add the sidebar and monogram cover-letter layouts

Two new arrangements alongside Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy, each with a DOCX
approximation and an honest ATS-mode degradation.

Sidebar widens the left margin to 62mm, fills it with a pale accent rail, and
`place`s the letterhead (name/role/contact) into it; the correspondence runs in
ONE column beside it. The rail is a margin position, not a second column of
prose, so extraction still reads letterhead -> date -> recipient -> body ->
sign-off. `place` does not participate in layout, so the rail can never push the
body around or move a page break.

Monogram sets a pale accent square carrying up to two initials beside a
name/role/contact lockup, over a rule. The square is pale-fill with accent ink
rather than a saturated tile with white text, because the accent comes from
whichever resume template is active and a light accent would put white on
near-white -- and the 85% lightening is the same `band_tint_hex` the DOCX side
already uses, which is what lets the two formats show one tint.

The brief said to mirror how Banded gates its band under ats_mode. It does not:
`ats_mode` never reached the letter path at all. `render_letter_pdf` had no
`ats` parameter, `LetterOpts` had no `ats` field, and `pdf/mod.rs` read
`request.ats_mode` for resumes only -- so a user who turned the toggle on still
exported a banded cover letter with its band. That is threaded now, as
`data.opts.ats`, and Banded's band is gated on it too: the discipline has to be
uniform or the toggle is a lie. Under ATS mode Sidebar drops the rail and stacks
the letterhead in one plain column, Monogram drops the device entirely (its
initials are real text -- extraction read "JS Jane Smith", two characters of
noise ahead of the candidate's own name), and Banded drops the band. No layout
adds or removes a WORD either way, which is what the tests assert alongside the
missing fill.

`ats` is a required parameter on `parse_cover_letter` rather than a defaulted
field: an ATS toggle that silently fails to reach the renderer looks exactly
like one that works, which is how this gap survived four letter layouts.

reusing the rule letter_refined.typ and letter_navy.typ already carry —
`strip-subject-label` on the body, and suppress the caption when the subject
still carries a marker of its own. That is also what the DOCX renderer does in
`strip_market_label`, so the PDF and DOCX sides now agree; they did not before,
which is the part that made this more than cosmetic.

`subj-used` gating is untouched: whether a subject renders AT ALL stays the
market's call (US omits it), and that is a separate question from how it renders
once the market has asked for one.

* test(export): close the two gaps that let the duplicate de label ship

Both gaps were named in the review and both were real.

(a) The PDF market-gating test asserted `de.contains("betreff")`, which is
satisfied by one label and by two. Now an occurrence COUNT of exactly one.

The count alone turned out not to be enough, and the mutation run is what showed
it: reverting the strip left the test GREEN, because the caption-suppression
guard independently hides the caption once the body still carries its label —
one occurrence either way. Added the assertion that says WHICH occurrence
survived: the colon only exists on an unstripped body, so `not
contains("betreff: bewerbung")` pins that the caption is what remains.

(b) No DOCX test had ever used a market with a subject label — every
`letter_request` passes `locale: None`, which resolves to label-less `intl`. So
the DOCX suppression rule was running untested, and with neither side covered
the two formats could disagree in silence. Added a DE case across all four
caption-bearing layouts, with the same count + colon assertions, which is now
the PDF/DOCX parity pin for this behaviour.

Mutation matrix, three ways: reverting the STRIP alone fails on the colon
assertion; reverting the CAPTION SUPPRESSION alone stays green; reverting BOTH
fails on the count with "found 2", reproducing the shipped defect. The middle
result is worth recording rather than hiding — with the strip in place the
suppression is unreachable for these two layouts in the current market set, so
it is defence for a future market, not live logic, and no honest test can
isolate it today. The DOCX test was mutation-checked separately against
`strip_market_label` and is not vacuous.

head_commit.message:
fix(autopilot): stop the double scroll when returning from an application (#987)

* fix(autopilot): stop the double scroll on back-to-autopilot from apply

Returning from an Apply via "back to autopilot" pushed a fresh /autopilot
navigation, so TanStack Router's own scrollRestoration ran first (reset/
restore to top), then AutopilotPage's focus effect re-expanded the source
card and scrollIntoView'd the applied job — two visible scroll motions
instead of one. Skip the router's scroll pass for that one hop
(navigate({ resetScroll: false })) only when from === 'autopilot', so the
app-level focus effect is the sole scroll motion. Other back targets keep
the default reset-to-top (they have no compensating scroll effect).

* fix(autopilot): gate the scroll-reset skip on pending focus, not just origin

frontend-reviewer MEDIUM: the from=autopilot search param survives native
forward-navigation (mouse forward / Alt+Right), while lastAppliedId is a
one-shot session-store field consumed on AutopilotPage's next mount. A
second arrival at ?from=autopilot with no pending focus left silently
dropped the router's default scroll reset with nothing compensating.
Read lastAppliedId from the session store and require both from ===
'autopilot' AND a pending id before skipping restoration; otherwise fall
back to the default reset. Also notes (LOW) that back() trusts `from` only
because the state gate enforces it, even though routes/__root.tsx and
use-notifications.ts pass backend-supplied search straight to navigate().
